subject.title: RFC: Period-based popularity for publishers, skills, and plugins

question: Should ClawHub first define and build the shared weekly/monthly publisher, skill, and plugin leaderboard contract, or should it expose only the current narrower trending surfaces?
rationale: Current main partially covers skill and plugin trending, but lacks publisher temporal rollups, monthly semantics, snapshot-pinned period pagination, and scoring/attribution decisions; automation cannot choose that product/data contract safely.

options.title: Build shared foundation first
options.body: Define scoring, trailing windows, attribution, backfill or warm-up policy, and snapshot retention before adding tabs across creators, skills, and plugins.

options.title: Expose only current trending
options.body: Limit UI to clearly labeled existing skill/plugin trending and leave publisher period popularity out until publisher rollups exist.

options.title: Defer period tabs
options.body: Keep current browse surfaces while maintainers collect more product signal on scoring and low-activity behavior.

recommendation.title: Build shared foundation first
recommendation.body: Define scoring, trailing windows, attribution, backfill or warm-up policy, and snapshot retention before adding tabs across creators, skills, and plugins.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the RFC and have direct feature-history ties to the publishers/creators discovery surface that anchors the user-facing request.
